clue.text: Not the whole of trial can collapse

indicators.note: when a structure collapses it falls into pieces that lie in a new jumble, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone warns that part of a court case may fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening phrase; 'of' belongs to the fodder, not the link, giving the ten letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something partial, only a portion rather than complete, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Notice worker accepting project for military assistant

indicators.note: the outer pieces take in the next one, as a host accepts a guest

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a notice
an ant is the classic worker insect
to project is to jut out

explanation.surface: An advert for a labourer working on a scheme to help the army.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer who assists a commanding officer with administration holds this title.

clue.text: Oddly veined salad plant

indicators.note: set out oddly, the letters of veined come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A leaf with peculiar veins sits in the salad bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but that gives only three; here it signals a rearrangement of all six.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter leafy chicory grown for salads goes by this name.

clue.text: You may meet one, if coming up north more than once

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned

indicators.note: the abbreviation appears twice over, more than a single time

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A traveller heading up north repeatedly may bump into someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is vague on purpose: head far enough north, to Finland, and you may well meet a native.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Finland, whom a northern traveller might encounter, is one of these.

clue.text: Pub needs approval for modernisation

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is applause, a show of approval

explanation.surface: A tired pub must win public favour to get its refurbishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing new methods or ideas is synonymous with making things modern.

clue.text: Plant in Grade A condition

indicators.note: to condition something is to work it into a new state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant is in top-notch shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grade A condition' reads as one phrase meaning excellent; 'condition' is actually the anagram signal acting on IN and GRADE A.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant white-flowered evergreen shrub is a well-known example of a plant.

clue.text: The cad is out to break the engagement

indicators.note: a thing that is out is disordered or off, so these letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A cad has been found out and the wedding is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface engagement is a betrothal; the definition means separate or disengage, as troops withdraw from contact.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or disengage, unfastening one thing from another, matches breaking an engagement.

clue.text: Autumn trip over

definitions.meaning: the American name for the season after summer
to stumble and tumble to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The North American word for the season is this, and so is a verb for stumbling to the ground.

clue.text: Communist officer seen on a merchant ship

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a communist
an ensign is a junior naval or army officer

explanation.surface: A communist officer is spotted aboard a trading vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the British merchant navy flies this flag, nicknamed the 'Red Duster'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag flown by British merchant vessels is this red banner with the Union flag in its corner.

clue.text: Scene of combat in an era that was backward

indicators.note: these words are read from the end back to the start
the letters sit within the words that follow, an era

explanation.surface: A battle took place in a less advanced period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators fought in an amphitheatre's central space, so it is a classic place of combat.

clue.text: Warn one that's amusing

definitions.meaning: to give someone a formal admonition, as police do
an informal word for a person who is a real laugh

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to admonish, and informally the noun names a very funny person.

clue.text: Not even graduate students can be so bizarre

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
L is a learner; two of them make students

explanation.surface: Uneven numbers of graduates and students turn out weird.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates on a British learner driver's car; doubled it means several students.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word describes something strange or eccentric.

clue.text: Bad sailor losing his head, gets angry

indicators.note: the first letter of the sailor is dropped

parts.note: a pirate is a criminal seaman

explanation.surface: A wicked seaman, beheaded, is understandably furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious or very cross is a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Arrested resolute pressman

parts.note: staunch means firmly loyal and determined
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A determined journalist was taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrested' looks like police work, but here it means stopped, as a flow of blood is.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt the flow of blood is to stem it; arrested here means stopped.

clue.text: Their speech is never straightforward

parts.note: suggests evasive speakers, but means people whose words come out haltingly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at politicians who never give a direct answer; the real people simply repeat sounds as they talk.
explanation.definitionFit: People with a speech impediment that repeats syllables never speak smoothly.

clue.text: Female serving the school

parts.note: suggests a woman devoted to an institution, but means one who dishes out lunches

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the woman who serves school lunches is known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to serve midday meals to schoolchildren is literally serving the school.

clue.text: Antonio's Italian variety of public ownership

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters are made into another arrangement

explanation.surface: An Italian named Antonio favours a particular form of state control.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking industries into state control places them under public ownership.

clue.text: Shrub no dealer can provide

indicators.note: these letters can be rearranged to supply the plant, as a supplier provides it

explanation.surface: A shrub that no plant seller is able to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous evergreen with pink or white flowers is an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Head off from Wyoming in terrible disgrace

indicators.note: a terrible state is a mess, so the letters are scrambled
the first letter of Wyoming is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone leaves Wyoming in deep shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off from' removes W, leaving YOMING; 'terrible' then rearranges YOMING with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Public shame or dishonour is a synonym of disgrace.

clue.text: One fond of the girls puts damsel in a turmoil

indicators.note: putting the letters into turmoil throws them into disorder

explanation.surface: A womaniser throws a young woman into confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like part of the indicator 'in a turmoil', but those letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who enjoys and courts women's company is described by this phrase.

clue.text: How to amuse people other than motorists?

definitions.text: How to amuse people other than motorists?

parts.words: How to amuse people other than motorists?
parts.note: the verb means to entertain, except for drivers, for whom it means sending them another way

explanation.walkthrough: For drivers the word means rerouting traffic; for everyone else it means entertain.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone is one sense, while sending traffic on another route is the motorist's sense.

clue.text: Fight to protect one's property

definitions.meaning: to duel with swords as a sport
to enclose land with a barrier

explanation.definitionFit: Swordplay is one meaning; putting a barrier around land to guard it is the other.

clue.text: Though in favour of an offer, say no

parts.note: for means supporting
a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: Someone likes a proposal yet still turns it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit or refuse permission is to say no.

clue.text: You'd be well advised to accept his spot judgment

definitions.text: You'd be well advised to accept his spot judgment

parts.words: You'd be well advised to accept his spot judgment
parts.note: well means a water well: this person decides the spot where one should be dug

explanation.walkthrough: 'well advised' reads as 'sensible', but it means advised about a well; 'spot judgment' is his choice of the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser who locates underground water with a rod picks where a well should go.

clue.text: Fed up youth's first to resist

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top
only the opening letter of the word youth's is used

explanation.surface: A young person who is fed up begins to rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To openly resist or disobey is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: A sweet shade of brown

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a chewy burnt-sugar confection and the light brown colour of that sugar.

clue.text: Overcook fish

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blacken by cooking too long
a trout-like fish of cold lakes

explanation.definitionFit: To scorch food is one meaning; a salmon-family freshwater fish is the other.

clue.text: It was used to make links at Gretna Green

definitions.text: It was used to make links at Gretna Green

parts.words: It was used to make links at Gretna Green
parts.note: links are chain links from a smithy, and also marriages made there by the blacksmith

explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, was famous for runaway weddings performed by the village blacksmith over his anvil.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's workshop makes metal links, and at Gretna Green the smithy also joined couples.

clue.text: Changed positions on parade again?

parts.note: soldiers on parade line up; doing it once more puts them back in line

explanation.walkthrough: The word normally means changed one's stance or alliance; read literally, it is soldiers lined up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting a stance or allegiance is the usual sense; literally it is putting into line once more.
